title: The 'scope of the sky
caption: An Auxiliary Telescope under the Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: One of the four Auxiliary Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope sits beneath the arc of the Milky Way at Paranal Observatory.

The excellent observing conditions at Paranal, together with the VLT's advanced technology, let astronomers study the Universe in detail. Each Auxiliary Telescope is 1.8 meters across, and they send their light into the VLT Interferometer, or VLTI, which combines light from several telescopes to sharpen the resolution even more and produce crisper images of astronomical objects.

The Auxiliary Telescopes are not fixed in place. They can be moved along tracks to many positions on the VLT platform. That flexibility lets astronomers adjust the VLTI to fit what each observing project requires, rather than working with a single fixed arrangement of telescopes every night.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye can, so the Milky Way and faint stars appear brighter and richer than they would to someone standing there.

explore: The photograph was taken by A. Ghizzi Panizza. The Milky Way overhead is our own galaxy, seen from within as a glowing band across the sky, made of countless stars along with clouds of gas and dust.
